newsitem.title: CHINA: China securities punishment short of expectation.
newsitem.headline: China securities punishment short of expectation.

text.p: Punishment meted out by China's financial authorities in recent days to banks and securities houses breaking the rules on stock trading has been much lighter than investors expected, brokers said on Monday.
Late last week, the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) announced punishments for more a dozen banks and securities houses for irregularities on the stock market.

Rumours that the securities authorities would crack down on stock trading had sharply reined in Shanghai's A share market bull-run in recent weeks, but on Monday, the market's A share index ended up 57.943 points or 5.79 percent at 1058.829.
"The outcome was much less serious than investors had expected," said one broker. "Investors believe there will be no more negative news."

In the biggest case, the CSRC imposed a fine of 1.13 million yuan ($136,000) on a branch of the Guangdong Development Bank for illegally using funds to bid for shares in a company to be listed on the Shenzhen stock market, the China Securities said on Saturday.
Shanghai brokers said they believed the punishments were the beginning of a campaign by the authorities to impose greater discipline of China's young and volatile financial markets.

"This is just a start to the crackdown on excessive speculation on the stock market," one broker said. "In the long run, the punishments will help to reduce the boom-and-bust syndrome in the markets."
